questions.questionText: Which accounting concept states that a business and its owner are treated as separate legal/financial units?
questions.explanation: Business entity separates personal transactions of the owner from business records.

questions.questionText: Under the prudence concept, inventory (closing stock) must be valued in the balance sheet at:

options.text: The lower of cost and net realisable value

questions.explanation: Prudence avoids overstating assets by taking the lower of cost and NRV.

questions.questionText: A sole trader purchases machinery on credit from Harare Engineering Ltd. Which book of original entry records this transaction?
questions.explanation: Credit purchase of non-current assets (not goods for resale) is recorded in the General Journal.

questions.questionText: Which document does a seller send to a customer when goods sold on credit are returned as damaged?
questions.explanation: A Credit Note reduces the amount owed by the customer upon sales returns.

questions.questionText: What is the double entry when the owner takes goods costing $150 from the business for personal family use?
questions.explanation: Owner taking stock reduces Purchases (at cost) and increases Drawings.

questions.questionText: A petty cash imprest float is fixed at $200. At month end, vouchers total $164. How much cash is reimbursed to restore the imprest?
questions.explanation: Under the imprest system, reimbursement equals exact cash spent ($164) to restore $36 + $164 = $200.

questions.questionText: Which error will NOT cause a Trial Balance to disagree?

options.text: Adding up the Sales column wrongly by $100
Posting $500 wages to the Motor Expenses account by mistake
Omitting the Cash balance from the Trial Balance

questions.explanation: Error of commission posts the correct debit and credit amounts to the wrong nominal account of the same class, keeping totals equal.

questions.questionText: Which item appears on the debit side of a Sales Ledger Control Account (Total Trade Receivables)?
questions.explanation: Credit sales increase amounts owed by debtors (Debit Control A/c).

questions.questionText: When preparing a Bank Reconciliation Statement starting with the Cash Book balance, an unpresented cheque of $420 should be:

options.text: Deducted from Bank Statement balance only
Written off as a bad debt

questions.explanation: Cheques already credited in Cash Book but not yet cleared by bank make Bank Statement higher: Cash Book + unpresented cheques - uncredited deposits = Bank Statement.

questions.questionText: A machine bought for $10,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum using the reducing balance method. Calculate the depreciation charge in Year 2.
Rent prepaid by a business at the end of the financial year is shown in the Statement of Financial Position as:
questions.explanation: Prepaid expenses represent value paid in advance for next period (Current Asset).

questions.questionText: At year-end, trade receivables are $12,000 after writing off $500 bad debts. A 5% provision for doubtful debts is required. What is the new provision?
questions.explanation: Provision is calculated on remaining good debtors: 5% × $12,000 = $600.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is classified as Capital Expenditure?

options.text: Buying and installing a new factory generator
Replacing worn spark plugs in a delivery van

questions.explanation: Acquiring and installing a new long-term non-current asset is capital expenditure.

questions.questionText: Sales = $80,000, Opening Inventory = $9,000, Purchases = $52,000, Closing Inventory = $11,000. Calculate Gross Profit.
In a partnership with no written Partnership Agreement, how are profits and losses shared?
questions.explanation: Under the Partnership Act, absent a deed, profits and losses are shared equally with no salaries or interest on capital.

questions.questionText: Where are partner salaries and interest on drawings recorded in partnership accounts?
questions.explanation: Salaries, interest on capital, interest on drawings, and profit shares appear in the Appropriation Account.

questions.questionText: In a non-profit Sports Club, what is the club's equivalent of "Owner's Capital"?
questions.explanation: Accumulated Fund = Total Club Assets minus Total Club Liabilities.

questions.questionText: Current Assets = $18,000 (including Inventory $6,000); Current Liabilities = $8,000. Calculate the Quick (Acid Test) Ratio.
questions.explanation: Acid Test = (Current Assets - Inventory) / Current Liabilities = (18,000 - 6,000) / 8,000 = 12,000 / 8,000 = 1.50 : 1.

questions.questionText: In a Manufacturing Account, Prime Cost equals:

options.text: Direct materials + Direct labour + Direct expenses

questions.explanation: Prime cost sums all direct costs of production.

questions.questionText: Carriage inwards on goods bought for resale is included in:

options.text: Trading Account as part of Cost of Goods Sold

questions.explanation: Carriage inwards increases cost of purchases in the Trading section; carriage outwards is an operating expense.

questions.questionText: When a cheque received from a debtor is returned by the bank marked "Refer to Drawer" (dishonoured), the double entry is:
questions.explanation: Dishonoured cheque reverses the receipt: reinstate debtor (Dr Debtor) and reduce bank (Cr Bank).

questions.questionText: Which ratio measures how efficiently a shop turns over its stock during the year?
questions.explanation: Rate of Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold / Average Inventory.

questions.questionText: Credit purchases during the year can be calculated from incomplete records using:
questions.explanation: Reconstructing Total Trade Payables Control Account reveals missing credit purchases.

questions.questionText: A suspense account had a debit balance of $350 before errors were found. It was discovered that Discount Allowed $175 had been credited instead of debited to the Discount Allowed account. Does correcting this clear the suspense account?

options.text: No, it doubles the balance to $700
Yes, Dr Suspense $350, Cr Discount Allowed $350
Yes, correction is Dr Discount Allowed $350, Cr Suspense $350

questions.explanation: Posting $175 to wrong side causes a $350 imbalance; Dr Discount Allowed $350 & Cr Suspense $350 clears it completely.

questions.questionText: Subscriptions received in advance from club members at year end appear in the club's Statement of Financial Position as:
questions.explanation: Prepaid income owed in future service to members is a Current Liability.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of a Cash Discount offered to credit customers?

options.text: To encourage prompt payment before the credit period expires

questions.explanation: Trade discount encourages bulk trade; cash discount rewards early settlement.

questions.questionText: In a departmental Income Statement, how should factory/shop rent expense normally be apportioned between departments?

options.text: In proportion to number of staff
In proportion to floor area occupied

questions.explanation: Rent relates directly to space occupied -> apportioned by floor area.

questions.questionText: Cost of Goods Sold = $45,000 and business applies a uniform 25% mark-up on cost. Find Sales revenue.
Which accounting document lists all debit and credit ledger balances at a given date to check arithmetic accuracy?
questions.explanation: A Trial Balance verifies that total debits equal total credits in the double-entry ledger.

questions.questionText: Opening Capital = $25,000, Drawings = $4,000, Additional Capital Introduced = $3,000, Closing Capital = $31,000. Calculate Net Profit.
questions.explanation: Closing Capital = Opening + Net Profit + Added Capital - Drawings -> 31,000 = 25,000 + NP + 3,000 - 4,000 -> NP = $7,000.
